sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: React fundamentals get you through the first round; the ecosystem knowledge gets you through the second. Interviewers for fullstack roles specifically check React Router (can you build a multi-page app), Context API (can you share state without prop drilling), and the performance hooks (do you understand when and why to memoize). Custom hooks are also a strong signal of practical experience — they show you can abstract logic, not just write components.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
- **React Router v6**: every route is a `<Route>` inside `<Routes>`; navigation uses `useNavigate()` hook not history object; params via `useParams()`.
- **Context API**: creates a global store without a library; best for low-frequency updates (theme, auth, locale) — not for frequently updating values.
- **useReducer**: like Redux but local; pairs with Context for complex state — `dispatch({ type: 'INCREMENT' })` pattern.
- **Custom hooks**: any function starting with `use` that calls other hooks. Extract reusable logic (data fetching, localStorage, form handling).
- **useMemo**: caches a computed value; re-computes only when dependencies change.
- **useCallback**: caches a function reference; prevents child re-renders when the function is passed as a prop.
- **useRef**: holds a mutable value that doesn't trigger re-renders; also for DOM element references.

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body:
- **react-router-basics**: `<Routes>/<Route>`, `<Link>`, `useParams`, `useNavigate`, and protected routes pattern.
- **context-api-and-usereducer**: `createContext`, `useContext`, Provider pattern, when Context is NOT the right tool.
- **custom-hooks**: rules of hooks (only call from components or custom hooks, only at top level), and a useFetch implementation.
- **api-calls-in-react**: useEffect + fetch pattern, loading/error/data state triple, AbortController for cleanup.
- **useref-usememo-usecallback**: know each purpose, know when NOT to over-optimize with them.
- **controlled-vs-uncontrolled-forms**: controlled with useState, uncontrolled with useRef, when each is appropriate.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- *"How do you implement authentication-protected routes in React Router?"* — wrap route element in a component that checks auth state and redirects with `<Navigate>` if not authenticated.
- *"When would you use Context API vs lifting state up vs Redux?"* — local UI state → useState; sibling components → lift state up; global/cross-cutting concerns (auth, theme) → Context; complex high-frequency state → Redux/Zustand.
- *"What is a custom hook and give an example?"* — a function starting with `use` that encapsulates reusable stateful logic, like `useFetch(url)` that manages loading/data/error state.
- *"When should you use `useMemo` vs `useCallback`?"* — `useMemo` for expensive value computations; `useCallback` for stable function references passed as props to memoized children.
- *"How do you cancel a fetch request when a component unmounts?"* — useEffect cleanup function with `AbortController`.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"In a fullstack project I connect React to a Spring Boot API using a custom `useFetch` hook that wraps useEffect with fetch, manages loading/error/data state, and cleans up inflight requests with AbortController on unmount. For navigation I use React Router v6 with protected routes that redirect unauthenticated users to the login page. Global auth state lives in a Context + useReducer store — because auth changes infrequently and needs to be accessible everywhere. I only reach for useMemo or useCallback when I've identified an actual performance bottleneck, not as a default."*
